s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic cutaneous nodular syndrome with systemic implications
salient_findings: Mild hypoaesthesia on the extensor side of the knee and ankle
Nodular infiltrates of foamy histiocytes in dermis
key_facts: One-year history of painless discrete cutaneous nodules
Nodules appeared on the limbs, trunk, and face
No fevers, joint pain, or hair loss reported
Family history negative for skin or autoimmune disease
Previous treatment with hydroxychloroquine, thalidomide, and topical steroids without improvement
Nodular infiltrates of foamy histiocytes in dermis arranged in storiform pattern

shortlist.label: Leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: Abundant acid-fast bacilli within histiocytes and epidermal atrophy

shortlist.label: Lepromatous leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular infiltrates of foamy histiocytes in dermis and positive anti-nuclear antibodies

shortlist.label: Borderline leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of acid-fast bacilli and skin nodules

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium leprae infection
shortlist.why_kept: Acid-fast bacilli in skin biopsy and earlobe tissue fluid

raw.rationale: The presence of abundant acid-fast bacilli within histiocytes, epidermal atrophy, and nodular infiltrates of foamy histiocytes in dermis arranged in storiform pattern are characteristic of lepromatous leprosy. The patient's lack of response to previous treatments and the presence of multiple systemic symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leprosy
rejected.why: Too broad, as leprosy encompasses several forms, including lepromatous, borderline, and tuberculoid leprosy

rejected.label: Borderline leprosy
rejected.why: Typically presents with a mix of tuberculoid and lepromatous features, which is not the case here

rejected.label: Lucio leprosy
rejected.why: A rare form of leprosy that presents with necrotizing vasculitis and is not consistent with the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Mycobacterium leprae infection
rejected.why: Too general, as it refers to the causative agent of leprosy rather than a specific form of the disease
